title: Unsafe Deserialization via Marshal.load
platform_conditions: Ruby 3.x standard library (Marshal, Psych YAML); on Psych 4.x (bundled since Ruby 3.1) YAML.load is an alias for safe_load, while Psych 3.x (Ruby 2.7/3.0) YAML.load permits arbitrary object instantiation
security_mechanism: Marshal.load rebuilds the object graph named inside the byte stream, instantiating user-defined classes without running their initialize and then firing serialization hooks along the way, so attacker-chosen instances reach dangerous states and methods — the stdlib documentation itself warns Marshal data must never come from untrusted input. Psych's YAML.load on Psych 3.x resolves tags to arbitrary Ruby classes, giving the same primitive, while YAML.safe_load restricts resolution to permitted classes. The JSON gem's create_additions option likewise re-instantiates classes from json_class tags in the document.

source_sink_clues.source: Session/state cookies, queued or cached payloads, and any byte stream an attacker can write that reaches a load call.
source_sink_clues.sink: Marshal.load on untrusted bytes; YAML.load (Psych 3.x) without safe_load/permitted_classes; JSON.parse with create_additions: true

tracking_guards: Check that untrusted state uses a data-only format (JSON without create_additions) or YAML.safe_load with an explicit permitted_classes list; check that a signature/HMAC over the payload is verified before any load call and the key is not attacker-readable.
not_candidate_when: The bytes are produced and consumed within one trust domain with no network or shared-storage exposure, an HMAC/signature envelope is verified before loading, or safe_load permits only the expected primitive types so no attacker-chosen class can be instantiated.
